misconception_description: Student believes that a variable assigned an arithmetic expression containing other variables automatically updates its value when those variables change.

solutions.generated_code:
program MatriksIdentitas
kamus
  n, i, j, posisiDiagonal : integer
  baris : string
algoritma
  input(n)
  i <- 1
  posisiDiagonal <- i
  for i <- 1 to n do
    baris <- ""
    for j <- 1 to n do
      if j == posisiDiagonal then
        baris <- baris + "1 "
      else
        baris <- baris + "0 "
      endif
    endfor
    output(baris)
  endfor
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student believes that `diagonal_position = i` creates a binding where `diagonal_position` will automatically update as `i` changes. They set `diagonal_position = i` when `i = 0`, then expect it to track the value of `i` throughout the loop. In reality, `diagonal_position` stays 0, so every row will have 1 at position 0, resulting in [[1,0,0,...], [1,0,0,...], ...] instead of the correct identity matrix. The student genuinely thinks this is elegant code that "links" diagonal_position to i.
